newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rain brings relief to French sugar beets - planters.
newsitem.headline: Rain brings relief to French sugar beets - planters.

text.p: The weekend's rain will help speed up the development of France's sugar beets, which has been hampered by a persistent dry spell, farmers said on Monday.
But more rain was needed over the next few weeks to help replenish depleted water tables after a three-month drought, they said.

"We are relieved. Rain was light but steady across France's main production regions. This should improve germination conditions," an analyst for the French sugar beet planters federation CGB told Reuters.

Between Friday and Sunday some 10-15 millimetres of rain fell on key beet producing areas, he said. As of April 25 only 40 percent of the beets sown had reached above-ground development but the weekend rain should help make up for earlier delays.
"Last week we were very worried. But now things will go very fast. Our only concern is the possible return of a high-pressure system," he said.
Meteo France has predicted that dry weather would return by mid-week.

A persistent dry spell combined with nightly frost had raised concerns over crop damage. But the CGB analyst said frost damage might be marginal, and farmers might need to re-sow some one percent of the crop in the Aube region in eastern France.
The national sugar intervention board FIRS expects France to produce 4.20 million tonnes of beet sugar in 1997/98 against 4.226 million in 1996/97, mostly the result of lower sowings.
